# Sirach Chapter 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** A humble person's wisdom can raise them to honor; it can seat them among the great.

**11:2** Never judge by appearances — beauty is no basis for praise, nor ugliness for contempt.

**11:3** The bee is tiny among all that flies, yet its honey is the sweetest of all.

**11:4** Don't brag about your fine wardrobe or put on airs on your day of glory — God's works are astonishing, and much of what he does among people stays hidden.

**11:5** Many rulers have been toppled from their thrones, while someone no one ever considered has worn the crown.

**11:6** Many powerful figures have fallen in disgrace; famous people have been handed over into the power of others.

**11:7** Don't rush to accuse — look into the matter first, then speak.

**11:8** Don't answer before you've actually listened, and don't butt in while someone is still talking.

**11:9** Don't quarrel over something that's not your business, and don't join in when sinners are rendering judgment.

**11:10** My child, don't take on too much; if you pile up commitments, you'll pay for it. If you chase after everything, you'll catch nothing — you can't run fast enough to escape your own overextension.

**11:11** Some people push and strain and rush — and still fall further behind.

**11:12** Others are slow and weak, in need of help — yet the Lord notices them and lifts them out of their lowly place.

**11:13** He raises their heads, and people marvel at what has happened.

**11:14** Good and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth — they all come from the Lord.

**11:15** God's blessing stays with those who are faithful to him; his favor flourishes forever.

**11:16** One person gets rich through careful, steady effort — that is their reward.

**11:17** Another stays poor through excessive penny-pinching — that is their lot.

**11:18** There's someone who piles up wealth through sheer stinginess — and this is what they get for it:

**11:19** They say, "I can finally rest — now I'll enjoy what I've saved" — but they have no idea when they'll have to leave it all behind and die.

**11:20** Stay faithful to your commitment; keep at your work; grow old in it.

**11:21** Don't be awed by the success of a sinner — trust God and stick to your work; he can make a poor person rich in an instant.

**11:22** God's blessing is the reward of the faithful; in a moment, his blessing blooms.

**11:23** Don't say, "What do I really need? What's going to help me from here on out?"

**11:24** Don't say, "I've got enough — what could possibly go wrong?"

**11:25** When life is good, hard times are forgotten; when life is hard, good times fade from memory.

**11:26** But the Lord settles accounts at the end — it is easy for him to repay each person on their last day.

**11:27** An hour of suffering can wipe out a lifetime of pleasure; it is what a person does at the end that tells the real story.

**11:28** Don't declare anyone blessed before their death — only at the end will a person's true character be known, through both their deeds and their children.

**11:29** Don't open your door to just anyone — crafty people set all kinds of traps.

**11:30** A proud person is like a decoy bird in a cage — acting innocent while watching for your downfall.

**11:31** They twist what is good into something bad and put blame on anything worthy of praise.

**11:32** One small spark can start a great fire — and a sinner is always lying in wait for someone's blood.

**11:33** Watch out for someone with malicious intent — they scheme to hurt you and may leave a permanent mark on your reputation.

**11:34** Let a stranger into your home and they'll fill it with chaos, and you'll find yourself a stranger to your own family.
